**The meaning of the verses**
﴿وَعَلَى الثَّلَاثَةِ الَّذِينَ خُلِّفُوا﴾

And likewise Allah accepted the repentance of the three who were left behind from among the Ansar — they were Ka'b ibn Malik, Hilal ibn Umayyah and Murarah ibn ar-Rabi' — who stayed behind from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and grieved intensely, until the earth, vast as it is, felt narrow to them out of sorrow and regret for staying behind, and their own souls felt narrow to them because of the distress that befell them, and they were certain that there is no refuge from Allah except in Him. Then Allah, glorified and exalted is He, guided them to obedience and to returning to what pleases Him, glorified is He. Allah is the One who accepts the repentance of His servants, Merciful to them.

﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا اتَّقُوا اللَّهَ وَكُونُوا مَعَ الصَّادِقِينَ﴾

O you who have believed in Allah and His Messenger and acted by His law: carry out Allah's commands and avoid what He has forbidden in all that you do and leave, and be with those who are truthful in their oaths, their promises and all their affairs.

📖 At-Tafsir Al-Muyassar — King Fahd Complex.

**Talk with your child**
1. Why did Yazan keep quiet when the people blamed Rami? And what was his night like after that?
2. What did Abu Salim say when he gave the handkerchief back to Yazan? And what was the one thing he "still needed to do"?
3. Is it enough for the one who did wrong to confess in secret, if someone else was blamed because of him? (No; he clears the wronged person's name in front of those who heard the accusation, and puts right what he spoiled.)

**This week's exercise**
Agree with your child this week: whoever admits their mistake on their own is first thanked for their honesty, then puts right what they spoiled, and is not punished harshly. And if they really do admit it, keep the agreement with them, so they learn that honesty is nothing to be afraid of.
